title: Championship Round 2 - Advanced Theology & Universal Sciences
description: 50 high-difficulty questions: 25 Bible Knowledge + 25 General Knowledge.

questions.question_text: Which prophet was commanded to marry Gomer, the daughter of Diblaim, as a symbolic representation of Israel's unfaithfulness?
questions.explanation: God instructed Hosea to marry Gomer to portray Israel's spiritual unfaithfulness and God's persistent covenant love.

questions.question_text: Which king of Judah was struck with leprosy after unlawfully entering the temple to burn incense?
questions.explanation: Uzziah became angry with the priests who confronted him, and leprosy appeared on his forehead.

questions.question_text: Who interpreted the handwriting on the wall during Belshazzar's feast?
questions.explanation: Daniel interpreted Mene, Mene, Tekel, Upharsin, declaring that Babylon's kingdom had been numbered, weighed, and divided.

questions.question_text: Which judge killed six hundred Philistines with an oxgoad?
questions.explanation: Shamgar son of Anath struck down six hundred Philistines with an oxgoad and delivered Israel.

questions.question_text: Who was the high priest when the Book of the Law was discovered during the reign of Josiah?
questions.explanation: Hilkiah the high priest discovered the Book of the Law in the temple and gave it to Shaphan the scribe.

questions.question_text: Which prophet confronted King David after his sin involving Bathsheba and Uriah?
questions.explanation: Nathan confronted David through the parable of the rich man and the poor man's ewe lamb.

questions.question_text: Which son of Saul was secretly protected by David and later received a permanent place at the king's table?
questions.explanation: Mephibosheth, Jonathan's son, was shown kindness by David because of David's covenant with Jonathan.

questions.question_text: Which prophet saw a vision of a flying scroll measuring twenty cubits by ten cubits?
questions.explanation: Zechariah's sixth vision featured a flying scroll representing the curse going out over the land.

questions.question_text: Who was the priest of Midian and father-in-law of Moses?
questions.explanation: Jethro, also called Reuel in Exodus 2, was the priest of Midian and Moses' father-in-law.

questions.question_text: Which two craftsmen were specifically appointed and filled with the Spirit of God to construct the Tabernacle?
questions.explanation: Bezalel and Oholiab were endowed with wisdom, understanding, knowledge, and craftsmanship for the sanctuary's construction.

questions.question_text: Which king consulted the medium at Endor before his final battle against the Philistines?
questions.explanation: Saul disguised himself and sought the medium at Endor after the Lord did not answer him through the usual means.

questions.question_text: Which prophet was instructed to lie on his left side for 390 days and on his right side for 40 days?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel's symbolic actions represented the years of Israel's and Judah's iniquity.

questions.question_text: Who was the prophetess consulted by Hilkiah and the royal officials after the Book of the Law was discovered?
questions.explanation: Huldah delivered the prophetic message concerning the judgment coming upon Judah and the mercy shown to Josiah.

questions.question_text: Which apostle was selected to replace Judas Iscariot?
questions.explanation: After prayer and casting lots, Matthias was numbered with the eleven apostles.

questions.question_text: Which man fell from a third-story window while Paul was speaking at Troas?
questions.explanation: Eutychus fell asleep during Paul's prolonged teaching, fell from the third story, and was restored to life.

questions.question_text: Which individual was described as a runaway slave whom Paul sent back to Philemon?
questions.explanation: Paul appealed to Philemon to receive Onesimus no longer merely as a slave but as a beloved brother.

questions.question_text: Which king of Israel was rebuked by Jehu son of Hanani for helping King Ahab?
questions.explanation: Jehu questioned Jehoshaphat's alliance with wicked Ahab and asked whether he should help those who hate the Lord.

questions.question_text: Which priest raised the young Joash and helped overthrow Athaliah?
questions.explanation: Jehoiada protected Joash in the temple and organized his public coronation after Athaliah's reign.

questions.question_text: Which prophet declared that the righteous shall live by his faith?
questions.explanation: Habakkuk 2:4 contrasts the proud person with the righteous person who lives by faithfulness.

questions.question_text: Which woman concealed the Israelite spies in Jericho and hid them under stalks of flax?
questions.explanation: Rahab hid the spies on her roof beneath stalks of flax and helped them escape through her window.

questions.question_text: Which king of Judah burned Jeremiah's scroll column by column after hearing its contents?
questions.explanation: King Jehoiakim cut the scroll with a scribe's knife and threw its sections into the fire despite warnings.

questions.question_text: Who was the first Gentile convert whose household received the Holy Spirit during Peter's ministry?
questions.explanation: Cornelius, a Roman centurion, and his household received the Holy Spirit while Peter was preaching.

questions.question_text: Which prophet confronted Amaziah, the priest of Bethel, for opposing his prophecy against Israel?
questions.explanation: Amos rejected Amaziah's command to leave Bethel and prophesied judgment against his household.

questions.question_text: Which apostle was bitten by a viper on Malta but suffered no harm?
questions.explanation: A viper fastened onto Paul's hand while he gathered sticks, but he shook it into the fire and remained unharmed.

questions.question_text: Which Old Testament figure is identified as both king of Salem and priest of God Most High?
questions.explanation: Melchizedek blessed Abraham and received a tenth from him; Hebrews later develops his significance as a priestly type.

questions.question_text: What is the name of the boundary in a rotating black hole beyond which no observer can remain stationary relative to distant stars?
questions.explanation: The ergosphere is the region outside a rotating black hole's event horizon where frame dragging makes remaining stationary impossible.

questions.question_text: Which mathematician formulated the incompleteness theorems demonstrating limitations of formal axiomatic systems?
questions.explanation: Gödel's 1931 incompleteness theorems showed that sufficiently expressive consistent formal systems contain statements that cannot be proved within them.

questions.question_text: Which ancient civilization developed the Linear B writing system, primarily used to record an early form of Greek?
questions.explanation: Linear B was used by the Mycenaean civilization and deciphered by Michael Ventris in 1952.

questions.question_text: What is the name of the cosmic microwave background radiation's temperature anisotropy associated with the Sachs-Wolfe effect?
questions.explanation: The Sachs-Wolfe effect describes temperature fluctuations in the cosmic microwave background caused by gravitational potential differences encountered by photons.

questions.question_text: Which treaty formally ended the Thirty Years' War in 1648?
questions.explanation: The Peace of Westphalia consisted principally of the treaties of Münster and Osnabrück and ended the Thirty Years' War.

questions.question_text: Which physicist introduced the uncertainty principle as a foundational concept of quantum mechanics?
questions.explanation: Heisenberg's uncertainty principle establishes limits on the simultaneous precision with which certain pairs of physical observables can be known.

questions.question_text: Which philosopher wrote the Critique of Pure Reason?
questions.explanation: Kant's 1781 work investigates the limits and conditions of human knowledge, distinguishing phenomena from things in themselves.

questions.question_text: Which ancient Greek historian is traditionally regarded as the author of The History of the Peloponnesian War?
questions.explanation: Thucydides documented the conflict between Athens and Sparta and is noted for his critical historical method.

questions.question_text: Which element has the highest electronegativity on the Pauling scale?
questions.explanation: Fluorine has the highest Pauling electronegativity value, approximately 3.98.

questions.question_text: Which astronomer first provided observational evidence for the expansion of the universe through galaxy redshift measurements?
questions.explanation: Hubble's 1929 work established a relationship between galaxy distance and recession velocity, providing foundational observational evidence for cosmic expansion.

questions.question_text: What is the primary enzyme responsible for unwinding the DNA double helix during replication?
questions.explanation: DNA helicase separates the two strands of the double helix by disrupting hydrogen bonds between complementary bases.

questions.question_text: Which empire constructed the monumental city of Persepolis as a major ceremonial capital?
questions.explanation: Persepolis was founded under Darius I and developed as an important ceremonial center of the Achaemenid Persian Empire.

questions.question_text: Which literary work begins with the line 'Call me Ishmael'?

options.A: The Old Man and the Sea

questions.explanation: Herman Melville's Moby-Dick opens with the narrator introducing himself as Ishmael.

questions.question_text: Which economist is most closely associated with the concept of creative destruction?
questions.explanation: Schumpeter used creative destruction to describe how innovation transforms economies by replacing established products, firms, and production methods.

questions.question_text: What is the name of the limit beyond which a white dwarf cannot remain stable against gravitational collapse?
questions.explanation: The Chandrasekhar limit is approximately 1.4 solar masses; above it, electron degeneracy pressure cannot support a white dwarf.

questions.question_text: Which civilization developed the cuneiform writing system in ancient Mesopotamia?
questions.explanation: The Sumerians developed early cuneiform in Mesopotamia, initially for administrative and record-keeping purposes.

questions.question_text: Which scientist proposed the three laws of planetary motion?
questions.explanation: Kepler formulated three laws describing planetary orbits, including elliptical paths and the relationship between orbital periods and distances.

questions.question_text: Which battle in 732 is traditionally associated with Charles Martel halting an Umayyad military advance into Frankish territory?
questions.explanation: The Battle of Tours, also called the Battle of Poitiers, was fought between Frankish forces under Charles Martel and an Umayyad army.

questions.question_text: Which mathematical constant represents the base of the natural logarithm?
questions.explanation: Euler's number e is approximately 2.71828 and is the base of the natural logarithm.

questions.question_text: Which French philosopher wrote Being and Nothingness, a major work of existentialist philosophy?
questions.explanation: Sartre's 1943 philosophical work explores consciousness, freedom, nothingness, and human existence.

questions.question_text: What is the name of the process by which heavy elements are formed through rapid neutron capture in astrophysical environments?
questions.explanation: The rapid neutron-capture process, or r-process, produces many neutron-rich heavy nuclei, including elements such as gold and platinum.

questions.question_text: Which treaty divided newly encountered lands outside Europe between Spain and Portugal in 1494?
questions.explanation: The Treaty of Tordesillas established a demarcation line dividing Spanish and Portuguese claims to newly encountered territories.

questions.question_text: Which subatomic particle mediates the strong nuclear force between quarks?
questions.explanation: Gluons are the gauge bosons of quantum chromodynamics and mediate the strong interaction between quarks.

questions.question_text: Which novel by Fyodor Dostoevsky centers on Rodion Raskolnikov and his theory of extraordinary individuals?
questions.explanation: Crime and Punishment follows Raskolnikov, a former student who rationalizes murder through a theory of exceptional individuals.

questions.question_text: Which principle states that no two electrons in an atom can possess identical values for all four quantum numbers?
questions.explanation: The Pauli exclusion principle states that identical fermions cannot occupy the same quantum state simultaneously.
